styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden confessional with purple curtains, a lattice door and a carved cornice. Measured facts: 10 colours per tile (matches the hedge, below the stall at 17 and the well at 20), 18 distinct colours (far below the stall at 40 and the well at 38), 0% flat-fill coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted dark brown and not a black sticker line. Wood is shaded in about 4 steps (cornice highlight, mid brown, dark brown, deep), with grain on the panels. The curtains show only 2-3 purple steps and the door lattice is simple. It reads as clean and coherent, but it is thinner on colour variety and texture than the stall and well, with large smooth panel areas lacking per-plank grain or speckle. A careful artist would likely find it a little flatter than the richest references. Borderline, but with fewer ramp steps and a lower distinct-colour count than the same-kind references, I fail it.
